description: In Han China, lacquered leather was used for protective military equipment because lacquer helped stiffen the material, improve resistance to moisture, and increase durability. Leather scales or plates could be cut, shaped, pierced, and coated with repeated layers of lacquer before being laced together into flexible armor, sometimes alongside lacquered rawhide and other organic materials. These defenses were lighter than comparable metal armor and especially useful for infantry and cavalry, while their glossy black, red, or dark brown finishes also gave Han armor a distinctive appearance.
